items.root_cause: Env::declare_var always passes mutable: true, and Env::assign_raw syncs the write to the global object's mirrored property only when it is writable but unconditionally reports success either way, so a strict-mode assignment to a non-writable var-like global (undefined, NaN, Infinity) silently succeeded instead of throwing.
items.fix: Detect a var-like global binding via the pre-existing Env::global_binding_object and route the write through set_with_receiver (the object's own [[Set]], which already has correct per-property writable/getter/setter semantics), applying PutValue's strict/sloppy handling of an unsuccessful [[Set]] exactly as the Reference::Property arm does.

items.item: legacy platform object array-index vs named-property dispatch
items.root_cause: An array-index-shaped key that was not a currently supported index fell through to the named-property check (get/has), and any array-index key without an indexed setter/at all threw unconditionally instead of falling through to ordinary storage (set/define); delete for an unsupported index returned vacuous success (Some(true)) without ever deleting a real expando.
items.fix: get/has: an array-index-shaped key is never treated as a named property, in range or not; an unsupported index now falls straight through to ordinary own-property storage instead of being checked against named getters. set/define: gated purely on whether the interface has an indexed setter at all (matching WebIDL's actual [[Set]]/[[DefineOwnProperty]] algorithms), not on supported_index_count -- confirmed necessary by the existing optional_setters_and_deleter_receive_native_keys unit test, whose indexed_setter legitimately grows the collection at index == current length; no setter now falls through to an ordinary [[Set]]/[[DefineOwnProperty]] (Ok(false)) instead of throwing. delete: a supported index now correctly reports non-configurable delete failure (Some(false)); an unsupported index falls through to an ordinary [[Delete]] of any expando actually stored there (None), instead of silently claiming success without deleting anything.
items.target_test: dom/collections/HTMLCollection-supported-property-indices.html (5 subtests; WPT, not Test262 -- HTMLCollection-style legacy platform objects are a DOM/WebIDL concept with no Test262 coverage)
unit_test_updates: visibility_and_unenumerable_names_follow_hook_flags: index "8" (out of the fixture's 2-entry supported range, no indexed setter) now asserts a successful ordinary [[Set]] instead of an error.

optional_setters_and_deleter_receive_native_keys: unaffected by the corrected (setter-presence-gated) legacy_set/legacy_define now that the supported_index_count-based gate was reverted; this test is exactly what caught the initial over-eager range gate.

items.root_cause: A self-referential array (a.push(a); a.join()) converts its own element via ToString, re-entering join on the same array with no termination, overflowing the real Rust call stack (a process crash, not a catchable JS error).
items.fix: Thread-local identity stack (ARRAY_JOIN_STACK, keyed by std_weak_id) plus an RAII guard (ArrayJoinGuard) that pops on every exit path including early '?' returns; a re-entrant call on a currently-joining array contributes an empty string, matching observed browser behavior. Array.prototype.toString delegates to join through the interpreter and is covered by the same guard.

items.root_cause: Three multi-hop prototype-chain walks (ordinary_has_instance's own chain walk, set_prop's and binding_set_property's inherited-setter searches) read object.borrow().proto.clone() directly past the first hop, bypassing a Proxy or WindowProxy's getPrototypeOf trap for any hop beyond the first -- the specific gap flagged in JSRT-15's own TODO notes.
items.fix: Each loop now checks window_proxy_prototype then proxy_get_prototype before falling back to the raw proto read, matching the pattern already used elsewhere since JSRT-15.
